videos.script: You can send an answer back to the model that wrote it, and ask whether it is right. It sounds like a second opinion. It is the same reader, reading twice. {{review}} This lesson measures what that second reading catches. On seventy answers at temperature zero, it flags forty-five, and eighteen of them really are wrong. A check that flagged forty-five at random would do almost as well. {{table}} Then you read its reasons. Most say the JSON is missing a bracket, on replies that are complete. And the one reply that really is broken, it calls fine. {{misses}} Then you check a sampled run instead. There is a good argument that sampling should help a reviewer, and here it barely does. {{slips}} So the real checks go to code. A parser finds the broken reply every time, for free. {{argue}} By the end you know what to check with code, what to leave to a model, and how to measure the part you leave, against a coin. {{close}}
